name: Comprehensive Person Re-Identification Benchmark
description: Person re-identification (re-id) is a critical problem in video analytics applications such as security and surveillance. The public release of several datasets and code for vision algorithms has facilitated rapid progress in this area over the last few years. However, directly comparing re-id algorithms reported in the literature has become difficult since a wide variety of features, experimental protocols, and evaluation metrics are employed. In order to address this need, we present an extensive review and performance evaluation of single- and multi-shot re-id algorithms. The experimental protocol incorporates the most recent advances in both feature extraction and metric learning. To ensure a fair comparison, all of the approaches were implemented using a unified code library that includes 6 feature extraction algorithms and 21 metric learning and ranking techniques. All approaches were evaluated using a new large-scale dataset that closely mimics a real-world problem setting, in addition to 13 other publicly available datasets: VIPeR, GRID, CAVIAR, 3DPeS, PRID, V47, WARD, SAIVT-SoftBio, CUHK03, RAiD, iLIDSVID, HDA+ and Market1501. The evaluation codebase and results will be made publicly available for community use.
evaluation_method: mean Average Precision (mAP) and Cumulative Matching Characteristic (CMC) / rank-k accuracy (e.g., Rank-1)
general_score_metric: mean Average Precision (mAP) and Rank-1 accuracy
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark covering many public re-id datasets; evaluation is sensitive to protocol differences (feature/metric choices, train/test splits). Some datasets (e.g., Market1501) are approaching saturation while others remain challenging; not a small dataset but cross-dataset variability and differing protocols can complicate comparisons.
